sentences.text: Substation switching windows are coordinated with planned maintenance so that equipment is available only when the required operating conditions can be maintained.
The Duty Planner consolidates proposed work periods and identifies tasks that require a change to substation configuration.
The Maintenance Planning Engine checks task durations, dependencies, and resource assumptions before a window is proposed.
The Grid Dispatcher confirms that the requested period is compatible with export requirements and network operating limits.
The approved window includes a start time, an end time, the affected equipment, and the expected operating state.
The Substation Operator reviews the switching sequence and confirms that each step can be performed within the available interval.
The Control Engineer checks that turbine operations can be managed safely while the substation work is in progress.
The Grid Interface Relay remains available for the required protection and control functions throughout the planned work.
Work on the Main Transformer is scheduled only after its expected loading and required isolation duration have been reviewed.
Export capacity is assessed before any planned outage that could restrict power transfer.
A Grid Constraint may require the requested window to be shortened, moved, or divided into separate periods.
The final window allows time for switching, work execution, testing, and restoration without relying on unplanned extensions.
Weather Service forecasts are considered when marine access or external work affects the achievable start time.
The Marine Coordinator checks vessel movements and crew transfer timing against the proposed period.
The Electrical Technician confirms that the work scope and test requirements fit the approved duration.
The Work Permit Portal is updated to reflect the agreed timing and work boundaries before the activity begins.
Offshore Substation uses the Switching Window Acknowledgment to confirm that the approved switching window is available for the planned work.
The Substation Operator does not begin switching until the window is active and operational authority has been confirmed.
Any delay that threatens the agreed end time is raised promptly for review by the responsible operations staff.
Work is paused if actual conditions make the planned sequence unsafe or incompatible with grid requirements.
A revised window is agreed before deferred switching or additional maintenance is attempted.
Following completion, equipment is restored in the authorized sequence and its operating condition is checked.
The Duty Planner records actual start and finish times to improve future estimates and coordination.
Substation availability is returned to the operating plan only after restoration checks are complete and any remaining limitations are understood.
